NEW DELHI: India's medal tally climbed to six at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday, with shooters delivering three medals and Suchika Tariyal adding a historic bronze in mixed martial arts.Teenager Himanshu Dhillon won silver and former world champion Rudrankksh Patil claimed bronze in the men's 10m air rifle individual event. Their podium finishes came barely an hour after the duo, along with Parth Mane, had helped India win silver in the team event.Dhillon shot 252.4 points to finish behind China's Lihao Sheng (254.2), while Rudrankksh finished third with 230.9. Rudrankksh had led at stages of the final before Dhillon moved into second after a 10.6 in the sixth series.The three shooting medals took India's tally in the sport to five, after two silver medals on Sunday.Tariyal's bronze in the women's traditional 60kg MMA event was India's sixth medal and the country's first-ever Asian Games medal in the discipline, which is making its Games debut.Elsewhere, India defeated Japan 49-24 in men's kabaddi, beat Indonesia 17-1 in women's hockey, and defeated Pakistan 3-0 in women's table tennis.Boxer Sumit also advanced with a 5-0 win over Thailand's Bunjong Sinsiri.In swimming, Srihari Nataraj qualified for the men's 50m backstroke final. India’s women’s hockey team continued its goal-scoring spree at the Asian Games 2026, thrashing Indonesia 17-1 in their second Pool B match. After opening their campaign with a 19-0 demolition of Uzbekistan, the Women in Blue have now scored 36 goals in two matches, underlining their dominance in the tournament.Forwards Deepika Sehrawat, Rutuja Dadaso Pisal and Navneet Kaur each scored a hat-trick as India registered their second consecutive win. The victory also saw veteran goalkeeper Savita Punia make history by becoming the most-capped player in Indian women’s hockey, with her 321st senior international appearance.The 2023 Asian Games bronze medallists came out firing at the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium, scoring four goals in the opening quarter before adding five more in the second to take a commanding 9-0 lead at half-time.India maintained the pressure after the break, scoring five more goals in the third quarter and adding three in the final 15 minutes. Indonesia managed a consolation goal in the third quarter, but it did little to slow India’s attacking momentum.The win took India to six points from two Pool B matches, with a goal difference of 35.Deepika, Rutuja and Navneet led India’s scoring with three goals each. Deepika continued her impressive form after scoring eight goals against Uzbekistan in the tournament opener.Sunelita Toppo, Lalremsiami and Sakshi Rana contributed two goals apiece, while captain Salima Tete and Ishika Chaudhary also found the net. India opened the scoring through Deepika’s penalty-corner conversion in the eighth minute. Sunelita and Lalremsiami added goals before Rutuja scored in the closing moments of the first quarter.The Indian forwards continued to find openings in the second quarter, extending the lead to 9-0 by half-time. Indonesia scored through Innes Adiyita in the third quarter, but India responded quickly and kept piling on the goals.The match was also a landmark occasion for Savita Punia, who earned her 321st senior international cap to become the most-capped player in Indian women’s hockey history. The former India captain moved past Vandana Katariya, who held the previous record with 320 appearances. Savita’s milestone adds to a career that has seen her represent India at multiple major international tournaments.India will next take on Thailand in their third Pool B match on Wednesday as they look to maintain their winning run at the Asian Games. The women’s hockey competition also serves as a qualification pathway to the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.
Article Summary: India thrashed Indonesia 17-1 in their second Pool B match. Deepika Sehrawat, Rutuja Dadaso Pisal and Navneet Kaur each scored a hat-trick. Victory also saw Savita Punia make history by becoming the most-capped player in Indian women’s hockey.

Article Title: Asian Games 2026: Himanshu Dhillon wins silver, Rudrankksh Patil bags bronze in 10m air rifle
Article Text:
Himanshu Dhillion bagged silver in the 10m air rifle individual men's event.

India’s Himanshu Dhillon and Rudrankksh Patil added an individual silver and bronze, respectively, to the country’s shooting haul at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Monday, capping a memorable morning after the duo had earlier helped India win silver in the men’s 10m air rifle team event.Himanshu held his nerve through the seven-series final to finish second with a score of 252.4, while Rudrankksh ended with 230.9 for bronze. China’s reigning Olympic champion Sheng Lihao won the gold with 254.2, finishing 1.8 points ahead of Himanshu.The two Indians had entered the eight-shooter final after producing strong qualification scores earlier in the morning. Rudrankksh finished third in qualification with 631.8, while Himanshu was seventh with 630.0. Their qualification performances had already secured their places in the individual final and helped India to the team silver.Himanshu started the final strongly, scoring 52.2 in the opening series and moving to 104.8 after two series. He remained in medal contention throughout the elimination phase, eventually finishing second behind Sheng.Rudrankksh, meanwhile, opened with 52.8 and moved into the medal positions early in the final.He remained in the top three through the elimination rounds before finishing with 230.9.The individual medals came just hours after Rudrankksh, Himanshu and Parth Mane combined for 1890.1 points to win silver in the men’s 10m air rifle team event . China took gold with a world-record 1899.0, while South Korea won bronze with 1884.2.The double podium finish means all three Indian shooters who qualified for the team event contributed to a medal-winning performance, with Parth missing out on the individual final after finishing 10th in qualification.For Rudrankksh, the bronze adds another Asian Games medal to his collection after he was part of India’s gold-medal winning men’s 10m air rifle team at the Hangzhou Games. His latest medal also comes after he had won the individual gold at the Asian Rifle/Pistol Championships in New Delhi earlier this year.For Himanshu, the silver marks a major individual achievement at the Asian Games and comes in his first appearance in the competition's 10m air rifle individual final.India’s shooting campaign in Aichi-Nagoya has now produced a string of medals in the 10m air rifle events. Elavenil Valarivan had earlier won individual silver after also being part of India’s silver-winning women’s 10m air rifle team.With Himanshu’s silver and Rudrankksh’s bronze added to the team silver won earlier on Monday, India’s 10m air rifle campaign has delivered three medals in the men’s event alone.The result also strengthens the early momentum for an Indian shooting contingent that had produced a record 22 medals at the Hangzhou Asian Games, including seven golds.
Article Summary: Himanshu Dhillon and Rudrankksh Patil add individual silver and bronze to India's shooting haul at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. Duo had earlier helped India win silver in the men’s 10m air rifle team event.

From IIT Kanpur to Japan’s national cricket team, Abhishek Anand ’s journey has taken an unexpected turn and now, a viral video has put the Bihar-born cricketer in the spotlight ahead of Japan’s historic T20I against India.The 28-year-old, who hails from Bihar’s Rohtas district, moved to Japan for employment after completing his Chemistry degree at IIT Kanpur. He continued pursuing cricket alongside his professional career, eventually earning a place in Japan’s national team.However, despite the buzz surrounding his story, Abhishek’s participation in the September 22 fixture is not confirmed. Japan have announced a 15-member squad for the match, and Abhishek is not among the selected players.During his college years in IIT Kanpur, he remained connected to cricket and captained the institute’s team. After graduating, he relocated to Tokyo for work. Rather than giving up the sport, he began playing club cricket in Japan, balancing his professional commitments with his passion for the game.His performances in the local cricket circuit helped him earn a call-up to Japan’s national setup. Abhishek made his T20I debut against the Cook Islands on May 9, 2025.He has since played 18 T20Is, scoring 275 runs, including a highest score of 55, and taking one wicket, according to figures cited in recent reports.Abhishek’s journey has attracted attention on social media ahead of the India-Japan fixture, with a video fea turing the cricketer going viral. In the clip, he is asked about being a Bihari representing Japan. His response and a message directed at the Indian team have sparked interest among cricket fans, with the phrase “Bihari kahan nahi hai bhai” drawing particular attention.India and Japan are scheduled to meet in a historic one-off men’s T20I on September 22 at the Sano International Cricket Ground in Tochigi, Japan. Article Title: Once a daily-labourer, fourth-time Asiad campaigner Akash leads Indian squad buoyed by talent pipeline from Manipur
Article Text:
Indian sepak takraw men's team captain Akash Yumnam

Young Manipur players after winning during the state championships in 2026

Bihar's Bobby Kumar

KOLKATA: When India men’s sepak takraw captain Akash Yumnam steps onto the court in Nagoya on Monday, it will mark the latest chapter in a journey that has taken him from a daily-wage labourer in Manipur to a four-time Asian Games player.The veteran, who used to be a footballer and even spent a month training with NEROCA FC, is set to compete in his fourth Asian Games and remains one of only three members of India’s historic bronze medal-winning men’s regu team from the 2018 Games.But his path to the continental stage was far from straightforward.After losing his father, a government school teacher, in 2013, Akash suddenly found himself responsible for supporting his family. With no steady source of income, he worked as a daily-wage labourer, earning about Rs. 300 a day while continuing to train and pursue his sporting ambitions.“There was a period when I couldn’t even afford coaching expenses. I would work during the day and train in the evenings,” Akash recalled. “My mother, elder brother and younger brother depended on me, so I had to keep going.”The struggles lasted for a couple of years before he was recruited by the Sashastra Seema Bal through the sports quota in 2016.Today, he is not only one of India’s most experienced sepak takraw players but also the leader of a team aiming to return to the Asian Games podium.Akash’s rise mirrors the growth of the sport in Manipur, which continues to serve as the supply line for Indian sepak takraw. Manipur’s influence is evident in India’s Asian Games contingent, with five members of the men’s team and seven from the women’s squad hailing from the state.The state’s dominance was evident at the recent sub-junior nationals in Srinagar, where Manipur won five gold medals and a silver across six events.According to Manipur Sepak Takraw Association general secretary Ch. Geskant, Manipur’s proximity to traditional sepak takraw powerhouses such as Myanmar and Thailand played a key role in the game’s development.The growth has also been sustained by a strong club structure, with organisations such as Laipham Khunou Youth Development Association (LKYDA), Popular Union Club (PUC) and Youth Amateur Welfare Association (YAWA) nurturing generations of players.The state currently has more than 500 registered players, along with nearly 200 players in Under-12 category. The association is active across 13 districts and plans to expand grassroots competitions further.“We are particularly focused on the mini and sub-junior levels because that’s where future talent can be nurtured. There are nearly 200 players in the Under-12 age group and that is one area where we want to focus more attention,” Geskant said.Yet, sepak takraw’s footprint is gradually expanding beyond its northeastern stronghold. One example is Bihar’s Bobby Kumar, the only player from the state in India’s men’s squad. The 20-year-old from Patna discovered the sport at a local park near his home and progressed rapidly through the ranks despite initially knowing little about it.“I never imagined I would play at the Asian Games one day. I started because it looked interesting and gradually fell in love with the game,” he said.Bobby, who recently earned an appointment as a sub-inspector with Bihar Police, was also part of the Indian team that won gold at ISTAF Sepak Takraw World Cup final at Patliputra Sports Complex in Patna last year.India have continued their strong run this year, too, winning the Asian Sepak Takraw Championship title in Nagoya while also claiming a historic World Cup silver in Malaysia and a King’s Cup bronze in Thailand in the Quadrant event.Thanks to these performances, the squad, which has been training intensively in Sonipat for the past two years, is high on confidence ahead of the Asiad, and Akash believes a podium finish is certainly possible.“Our performances over the last two years have been very good. Earlier, we hoped to reach the later stages, but now we truly believe we can win medals,” said the captain.With Akash’s experience, Manipur’s thriving player pipeline and young talents such as Bobby emerging from new centres, India begin their journey in Nagoya with genuine belief that another Asian Games podium finish is within reach.
Article Summary: Akash Yumnam is set to compete in his fourth Asian Games. The veteran used to be a footballer and even spent a month training with NEROCA FC. His rise mirrors the growth of the sport in Manipur, which continues to serve as the supply line for Indian sepak takraw. Five members of the men's team and seven from the women's squad hailing from the state.

NEW DELHI: Hoping to build on the historic campaign three years back at Hangzhou, India begins its campaign at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya with a 500-plus athlete contingent, aiming to better the 106-medal tally racked up at the last Games.While the build-up to the Games has been marred by mismanagement, an accommodation crisis and the threat of a typhoon looming large over the Japanese prefecture, for the athletes, once the Games begin, it will be, as the adage goes, ‘game mode on’.The 500-plus athlete Indian contingent comprises a sizeable group of returning champions and experienced campaigners. 314 of those athletes are preparing for their first appearance at the continental event.Interestingly, women athletes make up 46.7% of the contingent. At 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is the youngest member. Equestrian rider Shruti Vora, 55, is the oldest.India will compete in 256 events across 36 of the 43 sports at Aichi-Nagoya, with the Games beginning on September 19 and running until October 4.Avinash Sable, returning from a year-long injury, will try to defend his men's 3000m steeplechase title, while Tajinderpal Singh Toor returns in the men's shot put.Parul Chaudhary will be another athlete trying to defend her women's 5000m crown, while India's men's 4x400m relay team will also go into the Games as defending champions.In badminton, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty will aim to defend their men's doubles title. Their gold in Hangzhou was India's first Asian Games title in the event.Indian compound archers swept all five gold medals in the discipline at Hangzhou, and returning champion Jyothi Surekha Vennam will be the fulcrum around whom India's archery campaign will revolve.Then there are athletes whose Asian Games story is still waiting for a first chapter.Mirabai Chanu has won a world title, Olympic silver and Commonwealth Games gold. The Asian Games medal remains missing from her collection.The 32-year-old will lead India's four-member weightlifting team in Aichi-Nagoya, with Gyaneshwari Yadav, Seram Nirupama Devi and Harjinder Kaur completing the squad.Chanu missed the 2018 Asian Games because of injury and did not compete at Hangzhou. Now, after a career that has already included a world championship title, an Olympic medal and multiple Commonwealth Games titles, the Asian Games is the major multi-sport medal still absent from her cabinet.Anahat Singh is another young Indian athlete arriving in Japan with a title already behind her.The 18-year-old is a World Junior Squash Champion and has made the transition from junior squash to the senior international circuit at a young age.She is part of India's eight-member squash team in Aichi-Nagoya. Joshana Chinappa, Tanvi Khanna and Shameena Riaz are the other members of the women's squad, while Abhay Singh, Velavan Senthilkumar, Veer Chotrani and Suraj Kumar Chand make up the men's team.Squash was among India's gold-medal sports at Hangzhou.Shooting will once again be one of the major sports to follow, with 27 events on India's programme.The contingent had bagged 22 medals at Hangzhou, including seven golds.Manu Bhaker returns in the women's squad alongside the in-form Esha Singh, Rahi Sarnobat, Elavenil Valarivan, Ashi Chouksey, Suruchi Singh and Tilottama Sen.The men's group includes Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar, Rudrankksh Patil and Anish Bhanwala.There will also be a sizable shotgun shooters' bunch, with the veteran Mairaj Ahmed Khan leading the pack alongside Kynan Chenai, Shapath Bharadwaj and Ahvar Rizvi. Neeru Dhanda, Manisha Keer, Maheshwari Chauhan and Parinaaz Dhaliwal are also part of the shotgun group.Neeraj Chopra, meanwhile, will not be in Japan. The javelin thrower, who defended his Asian Games title in Hangzhou, is missing the 2026 Games after an ankle ligament injury during training.Athletics has the largest athlete representation, with 78 competitors, and also has the biggest programme with 43 events. They had bagged a total of 29 medals, including six golds, at Hangzhou, and the expectation will be to go many a medal better this time around.Alongside Sable, Toor and Parul are names such as Gulveer Singh, Animesh Kujur, Harita Bhadra, Jyothi Yarraji, Murali Sreeshankar, Praveen Chithravel and Tejaswin Shankar.The men's hockey team goes into Aichi-Nagoya as the defending Asian Games champion, but its recent World Cup campaign has left a different question hanging over the side.India won gold in Hangzhou in 2023, beating Japan 5-1 in the final, and the title also secured direct qualification for the Paris Olympics. The team now has another Olympic berth at stake in Japan, with the Asian Games gold medallist earning direct qualification for Los Angeles 2028.The women's team comes to Japan with a more encouraging recent result.India finished fifth at the 2026 Women's Hockey World Cup, their best finish at the tournament in 52 years. The campaign included a 2-2 draw against China, the 2024 Olympic silver medallists, a result that carried particular weight after India's 4-0 defeat to the same opposition in the Hangzhou Asian Games semifinal.The women's team has not won the Asian Games since 1982, and gold in Aichi-Nagoya would also bring direct qualification for the 2028 Olympics. Salima Tete will captain the side, with Savita Punia, Lalremsiami, Navneet Kaur, Deepika and Nikki Pradhan among the experienced players in the squad.India's men's T20 team is led by Shreyas Iyer and includes Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson, Ishan Kishan, Shivam Dube, Tilak Varma, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Jasprit Bumrah and Arshdeep Singh.Sooryavanshi is also part of the squad.Harmanpreet Kaur leads the women's side, with Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Deepti Sharma, Richa Ghosh and Renuka Thakur among the selected players.India won both the men's and women's T20 gold medals at Hangzhou.There will also be Indian participation in four esports events - eFootball, Puyo Puyo Champions, League of Legends and Pokemon Unite.Haryana leads the state-wise numbersHaryana has the largest representation with 96 athletes.Maharashtra follows with 49, Tamil Nadu 37, Punjab 35, Manipur 34, Uttar Pradesh 32 and Delhi 30.Karnataka, Kerala and Madhya Pradesh have 24 athletes each.The representation stretches across the country, with athletes also coming from Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Arunachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Mizoram, Nagaland, Puducherry, Tripura, Sikkim, Ladakh and Lakshadweep.The support structure behind the contingent is spread across several programmes. National Coaching Camps account for 134 athletes, followed by TOPS Development with 78 and TOPS Core with 77. Khelo India has 65 athletes, TAGG 48 and National Centres of Excellence 25.Aichi-Nagoya therefore brings together a group that already knows the Asian Games podium and another that has never experienced it.Mirabai Chanu still has one major medal to add. Anahat Singh arrives as a world junior champion. Manu Bhaker and Aishwary Pratap lead another large shooting group, while Sable, Toor, Parul, Jyothi and Satwik-Chirag return as defending champions.And around them are 314 first-timers, spread across 256 events in 36 sports.
Article Summary: India will compete in 256 events across 36 of the 43 sports at Aichi-Nagoya, with the Games beginning on September 19 and running until October 4. The 500-plus athlete Indian contingent comprises a sizeable group of returning champions and experienced campaigners. At 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is the youngest member of the Indian contingent.

Article Title: Asian Games 2026: Typhoon Dujuan threatens Aichi-Nagoya as organisers postpone equestrian event
Article Text:
L-R: Asian Games football match; a flooded area following heavy rain as Typhoon Dujuan approaches Japan. (Reuters Photos)

Equestrian event postponed as storm approaches

A powerful typhoon approaching Japan's Pacific coast has raised concerns over possible disruption to the Asian Games 2026, with organisers taking a precautionary step by postponing the equestrian eventing competition as Typhoon Dujuan threatens to bring heavy rain and strong winds to parts of the country.The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) warned that conditions could deteriorate rapidly as Dujuan moves towards eastern Japan. The storm was expected to pass near the Boso Peninsula in Chiba Prefecture, east of Tokyo, on Monday evening, while heavy rain could continue through Tuesday.The agency also warned of the possibility of linear rainbands over parts of the Kanto-Koshin and Tokai regions. Such systems can produce intense rainfall over a concentrated area for several hours, increasing the risk of flash floods and landslides.Although the Aichi-Nagoya Games venues had not experienced significant adverse weather on Monday morning, organisers postponed the equestrian eventing competition from Monday to Tuesday as a precaution. The change was also linked to concerns over heavy rain and delays in preparing the riding arena.The wider weather situation has already affected transport in Japan, with parts of highways closed. Authorities have also warned of landslide and flooding risks in areas expected to receive the heaviest rain.For the Asian Games , the immediate impact remains focused on weather-sensitive outdoor events and transportation, while organisers continue monitoring conditions. Tokyo, which is hosting some Asian Games competitions, is also expected to experience the storm's effects.

Article Title: 'I'm hoping for gold': Star golfer Khalin Joshi backs India’s Asian Games golf teams for medal success
Article Text:
Khalin Joshi. (File Pic - TOI Photo)

NEW DELHI: With the Asian Games beginning in Japan's Aichi-Nagoya, golfer Khalin Joshi has backed India's men's and women's golf teams to challenge for medals.The men's squad features in-form professionals who have excelled both domestically and on the DP World Tour, while the women's team boasts experienced international campaigners.“We have a great team. Yuvraj has been playing excellent golf in Europe, Saptak is leading the Order of Merit, and all of them are riding high on confidence,” he said.“I'm really hopeful they're going to contend. I'm hoping for gold, and I just hope both the men's and women's teams keep the Indian flag flying high.”Joshi insists there has been no dramatic swing change, no new coach and no technical overhaul behind one of the ost consistent spells of his season. The Bengaluru golfer believes the biggest transformation has happened where scores are often decided in the mind.Fresh off his victory at the Nava Raipur Open on Friday, Joshi said “I haven't changed anything much, to be honest. I've just tried to work on my mental game and stay more in the present throughout the round.”That approach proved crucial in Raipur, where relentless rain forced officials to shorten the event to 36 holes.With only nine holes played on each of the final two days, golfers had little room for recovery, making fast starts essential.Rather than playing conservatively, Joshi embraced the conditions. “The moment we heard it was reduced to 36 holes, we knew we had to start from the get-go. Everyone had limited holes, so my mindset was to be aggressive,” he said.“The course was soft, which actually favoured attacking golf. You could hit your numbers and be more aggressive towards the flags.”The win comes at a time when Indian professional golf is enjoying unprecedented depth. Nearly every PGTI event this season has produced tightly contested leaderboards, with established names and emerging youngsters regularly challenging for titles.Joshi believes the increasing prize money and professionalism of the domestic circuit have fundamentally changed the competitive landscape. “The PGTI is very competitive now. We're very top-heavy and the top 20 to 25 players can win on any given week,” he said.He pointed to the current form of golfers including Saptak Talwar, Rashid Khan, Honey Baisoya, Akshay Sharma, Om Prakash Chouhan, Viraj Madappa, Kartik Singh, Kritish Batra and Shubham Jaglan as evidence of the circuit's strength. “People are working harder in the gym and on the golf course. Golf in India is growing by leaps and bounds, and it's only a matter of time before we see many more Indians succeeding internationally. ”While technical preparation remains important, Joshi's tournament routine is deliberately uncomplicated. The 33-year-old avoids adding pressure before decisive rounds and instead focuses on slowing everything down. “I sleep well before tournaments and try not to rush anything in the morning,” he said. “I give myself ample time for breakfast, warming up and getting to the tee. Whenever I hurry, things start going haywire. The key for me is to stay slow and just breeze into the first tee.”Interestingly, Joshi says he learns as much from conversations with contemporaries as from senior professionals. Among those he frequently discusses golf with is close friend and DP World Tour regular Shubhankar Sharma. “Shubhankar is a really good friend. We talk regularly about our games and what we're feeling,” Joshi revealed. “Honestly, I try to learn from everybody.It can be a senior player or even a youngster everyone has something valuable to offer. ”That openness extends to the increasingly close-knit atmosphere on the Indian tour, where fierce competition coexists with genuine camaraderie.Joshi believes that culture, combined with rising financial opportunities, is inspiring more young golfers to treat the sport as a viable profession.The Raipur champion has little time to celebrate. He returns to action this week at his home course, the Karnataka Golf Association, before a week's break ahead of the Tour Championship at Jaypee Greens and the lucrative DP World India Championship from Oct 15-18 at the Delhi Golf Club where only the top 24 players on the Order of Merit will tee up.For a golfer whose biggest victory this season was built on quieting the mind, the objective remains unchanged. “Just stay present everything else takes care of itself.”
Article Summary: Golfer Khalin Joshi has backed India's men's and women's golf teams to challenge for medals at the Asian Games. The 33-year-old is fresh off his victory at the Nava Raipur Open on Friday. He believes the increasing prize money and professionalism of the domestic circuit have fundamentally changed the competitive landscape.

BENGALURU: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is set to introduce a policy defining the scope of the Ombudsman and preventing its office from entertaining complaints concerning local or state-level matters, the TimesofIndia.com has learnt.The move is understood to aim at drawing a clearer line between issues that fall within the Ombudsman’s jurisdiction and those that the respective state associations should address first. Article Title: How one India T20I could become Japanese cricket's defining moment
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Alan Curr has stopped counting how many hats he's worn this week.On Sunday morning, with a typhoon on the horizon, the Japan Cricket Association (JCA) COO pulled covers off the wicket. Later, he was putting up hospitality tents, checking security plans and helping transform a quaint cricket ground with 500 permanent seats into a venue worthy of hosting the reigning T20I world champions. By Tuesday, weather permitting, India will walk out against Japan in the country's first-ever men's senior international against a Full Member.For Japanese cricket, getting here is success in itself and the scoreline almost secondary."A lot of success has almost already happened," Curr says. "The fact that India have agreed to come, the fact that I'm sitting here talking to you guys, the fact that Japanese media are coming to learn about cricket — we're having successes already," he told select media.Cricket is not new to Japan, having been introduced in the 1870s. But adaptation is a different story. Baseball, Football, Sumo Wrestling, Basketball, Golf, Tennis, Boxing are some sports that are bigger.India's arrival represents cricket's loudest introduction in recent memory.Japan has played in Under-19 World Cups, faced India and Pakistan at youth level and competed in the Asian Games with its women's team. But this is different gravy."It certainly helps to say that the reigning world champions, the No. 1 ranked team in the world, are coming to Japan," Curr says. "It's piquing interest, but we've still got a long way to go before cricket breaks into the mainstream sporting audience."That mainstream audience is precisely what the JCA hopes to reach. The timing is ideal: cricket returns to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya just days later, allowing Japan to explain the sport through one of the country's most recognisable sporting events."The Asian Games gives cricket legitimacy that it didn't have before," Curr says. "You can't be what you can't see."Behind the scenes, cricket has been expanding steadily in Japan. Registered players have risen from around 3,000 when Curr arrived in 2014 to 8,800 today. The Japan Cup -- the T20 competition in the country -- has grown from barely a dozen teams to more than 80, while the domestic 40-over league now spans four divisions."Kaizen is the word," Curr says. "Continual improvement. That's what we're trying to do for the sport. But now and again there are moments like this where you can accelerate that," he added.Japan harbour no illusions about the cricketing challenge ahead. "This India team is pretty good," Curr said as a matter of fact. "It's going to be an extremely difficult challenge for players who have never played at that level before."Instead, his measure of success is cultural.He points to Japan's women's team, praised recently for staying back after their Asian Games fixture against India to thank supporters and mingle with fans. That's the identity he wants the men's side to showcase too."We want cricket to be played hard but also be accessible and friendly," he says. "We want cricket to be fun."If thousands of first-time spectators leave Sano remembering more than just India's star power, Japanese cricket may have achieved exactly what it came for.The historic fixture was never part of Japan's grand plan to expand the sport. It began with clay.Eighteen months ago, the JCA set out to relay the turf square at Sano with help from Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC), whose groundsman travelled to Japan to identify suitable clay. The same surface was eventually used to build the Asian Games venue in Nagoya, prompting a simple thought: if Japan had international-quality wickets, why not invite the world's best teams to use them?Once the pitches were completed in March, Japan prepared a proposal and sent it to every Full Member ahead of the ICC conference in Edinburgh. Conversations with the BCCI began there — and, to Curr's surprise, moved quickly."The BCCI were really keen to have an opportunity to train. It's huge credit to them that they're excited about coming here and building this relationship with the JCA," he said.The timing made sense. With the Asian Games beginning days later, India men's squad would otherwise spend nearly a week waiting for their knockout fixture without access to proper cricket facilities. Sano offered both a training base and, eventually, a match. Again, with fingers crossed that the weather doesn't play spoilsport.India vs Japan T20I will be broadcast LIVE on FanCode on September 22 at 9:30 am IST.
Article Summary: Cricket is not new to Japan, having been introduced in the 1870s. By Tuesday, weather permitting, India will walk out against Japan in the country's first- ever men's senior international against a Full Member. Cricket returns to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya just days later, allowing Japan to explain the sport.

Fleming takes over after McCullum era

England’s recent Test victory over Pakistan has offered a timely boost as the team prepares for a new chapter under incoming head coach Stephen Fleming . But the former New Zealand captain has set his sights on a much bigger goal: taking England back to the top of the Test rankings and making the World Test Championship a central part of the team’s ambitions.Fleming addressed the media for the first time since being appointed England’s Test coach, describing the role as one of cricket’s most prestigious. He has signed a contract with the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) until September 2030, following a two-week recruitment process.“I would love to be in charge of the No. 1 Test team in the world. That would be my aspiration,” Fleming said, referring to England’s bid to reclaim the top spot for the first time since 2012.His first assignment will be a winter series against South Africa, followed by a home Ashes campaign, an occasion he said he has long admired as a New Zealander.Fleming said he has already begun working with Test captain Joe Root , with an emphasis on shaping England’s identity and building a strong sense of belonging within the squad.“The way players represent England and the group is going to be really important to me,” he said, adding that the team’s style of play would be shaped more by the players themselves.The World Test Championship is also high on Fleming’s agenda. England have yet to reach the final in any of the competition’s first three editions.“England could do much better than that,” he said, describing the WTC as an aspirational target alongside other major events. Fleming added that improving the team’s approach, including its over-rate, would be part of developing a clearer identity.Fleming succeeds Brendon McCullum , who had been in charge since 2022. England’s recent struggles over the past 18 months have formed part of the backdrop to the coaching change, though Fleming said he sees an opportunity to move the team forward.He said McCullum had been honest about the team’s situation and believed there was still potential within the group."That was one thing that will probably hurt him (McCullum) a little bit (underperformance) - I think he feels what I feel now, that there's an opportunity around the corner. He was also realistic about what had gone on and just very honest. It's interesting when you go to watch as a bystander for the first half of the year, then things change quite quickly to a real narrow focus on where the team was at,'' he said.

Smriti Mandhana scored 37 off 18 deliveries, while captain Harmanpreet Kaur contributed 40 off 33 balls.Bangladesh’s wickets were shared by Sanjida Akter Meghla, Marufa Akter, Nahida Akter and Rabeya Khatun, who took one apiece. Bangladesh need 196 runs to reach the gold-medal match against Sri Lanka.
Article Summary: Shafali Verma hits maiden white-ball century to guide India to 195/4 in Asian Games semifinal. Shafali has now struck 35 sixes in 2026, the most by any player in a calendar year.

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may still be only 15, but the sheer impact of his performances has already led to questions about whether he can eventually conquer all three formats. The Samastipur-born left-hander has made a stunning start to his career, with his exploits in the IPL and at the international level putting him firmly under the spotlight.His immediate future, however, remains in T20 cricket. Sooryavanshi did not feature in any of the matches, with Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma preferred at the top of the order. Given the team's desire to maintain continuity, the decision was understandable despite the teenager's impressive IPL campaign.The discussion has now moved beyond the teenager's place in India's T20I XI, with his potential in Test cricket becoming another talking point. Sooryavanshi has limited red-ball experience and is nowhere close to a Test call-up at present, but former England spinner Monty Panesar has already offered his assessment of whether the youngster can make the transition to the longest format.Speaking on the Beyond23 Cricket Podcast alongside former Australia captain Michael Clarke , Panesar questioned whether Sooryavanshi possesses the technique required to succeed in Test cricket.“I can’t see Sooryavanshi transitioning to Test cricket. Harry Brook is the only one right now who’s in the top 10 in Tests and T20Is. But I just don’t think Sooryavanshi has got the technique," Panesar said.Clarke, however, offered a contrasting view. The former Australia captain argued that players can succeed across all three formats if they have the necessary skill and talent, pointing to Virat Kohli and AB de Villiers as examples.“I think you can still play all three formats. Virat Kohli and AB de Villiers showed that. These guys were brilliant Test cricketers and unbelievable T20 cricketers as well. If a player from this generation, like Sooryavanshi, can make the transition into Test cricket, it is going to be unreal to watch," said Clarke.Clarke also highlighted Sooryavanshi's power and exceptional ability to read the ball as his biggest strengths at this stage of his career. He believes the technical aspects of the youngster's batting can develop with greater exposure to different conditions.“Right now, power is still his main thing, and he has an amazing eye. He picks the ball as well as any young cricketer in the world. The technique will get better the more he tours with India and trains in different conditions," said Sooryavanshi.Clarke went a step further in backing the teenager's long-term potential, suggesting he has the talent to become a star across formats if he chooses to pursue that route."He’s talented enough that, if he wants to do it, I can’t see any reason why he can’t be a superstar in all three formats," he added.Sooryavanshi has already had some exposure to red-ball cricket. He was part of the East Zone side that won the Duleep Trophy and came close to scoring a century in the semi-final against Central Zone before being dismissed in the 90s.
Article Summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has made a stunning start to his career. The 15-year-old has impressed in the IPL and at the international level. His immediate future remains in T20 cricket, but his potential in Test cricket is another talking point. Former England spinner Monty Panesar has questioned whether he can make the transition to the longest format.

MUMBAI: The BCCI’s position on the National Sports Governance Act dominated discussions at the board’s 95th annual general meeting on Friday, with secretary Devajit Saikia saying the body would comply with the law once cricket is officially notified as a designated sport.Saikia, however, said the BCCI would not come under the RTI Act because it does not receive govt grants. He said the board pays about Rs 3,000 crore annually in income tax, unlike other national sports federations that receive govt funding. “Regarding the Sports Act, our stand is very clear,” Saikia said after the AGM. “There are a lot of things yet to be done by the concerned authority. Once those exercises are completed, and once BCCI comes under the Sports Act, a notification has to be issued to make cricket a designated sport. Till that time, we are not supposed to do anything.”Saikia said the BCCI would respond to the Supreme Court on Oct 27, when the matter is next listed. “Whenever that notification comes, we will immediately act and do our work as per the rules of the new sports act.” Saikia also argued that cricket should not be treated like other govt-funded sports bodies. “We are paying 3,000 crore in tax annually to the govt. Unlike other sports federations, we don’t take any govt funding.Hence, cricket cannot be treated as a designated sport under the National Sports Governance Act 2025,” he said.The BCCI will complete 100 years in Dec 2028 and plans to form a committee for year-long centenary celebrations beginning in Dec 2027. Saikia said the board also discussed plans to mark the 20th edition of the IPL next year.“In Dec 2028, we will complete 100 years of the BCCI, so we will hold centenary celebrations from Dec 2027 for one year,” he said. “The IPL, which will start from March-end next year, will have its 20th edition. We have discussed that it should be done in a grand way.”
Article Summary: The BCCI will comply with the law once cricket is officially notified as a designated sport. Secretary Devajit Saikia said the BCCI would not come under the RTI Act because it does not receive govt grants. He said the board pays about Rs 3,000 crore annually in income tax.

Article Title: East Zone’s new cricketing core: How Bihar and Jharkhand talent powered Duleep Trophy win

East Zone team members (PTI Photo)

When South Zone and East Zone faced-off in the Duleep Trophy final, captain Tilak Varma’s team was widely considered as the favourite. South Zone were not only playing at home, but had added in-form batter Devdutt Paddikal and Test regular Mohammed Siraj to the playing XI. There was a difference in pedigree too. South Zone were 19-time winners and East Zone had taken home the inter-zonal trophy only twice, the last in 2012-13.But matches are not decided by reputation or history. East outplayed the hosts in every area, including hunger and self-belief to win the trophy. Even the sparse Chennai crowd clapped for the visiting side, especially for captain Ishan Kishan, a reborn cricketer whose monumental 270 first set an uphill task for Varma’s side, and whose feisty 80 shut the door on South’s faint revival hopes in the second.In the 1980s and earlier, East Zone were mostly also-rans in Duleep Trophy. The inter-zonal trophy began in 1961-62, but EZ won its first title only in 2011-12, with Wriddhiman Saha and Shami being the key to that triumph. Next season, Jharkhand’s underappreciated Ishank Jaggi’s ton fashioned East’s repeat success.Now, Jharkhand is a potent force in domestic cricket. In Dec 2025, the mineral-rich state claimed the T20 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy for the first time. Is it any surprise that Kishan scored a ton in the final and was Player of the Match, as in the Duleep Trophy final?Carved out of Bihar, Jharkhand became a separate state in 2000 — a reason why its biggest star, MS Dhoni, began his first-class career playing for (then) Rabri Devi ruled state in 1999.Kishan comes from Bihar, whose cricket association was mired in controversy for years. But several other Jharkhand players, who excelled with the bat in the Duleep final, are born and bred in the fledgling picturesque state. Kumar Kushagra, the 21-year-old ’keeper who stroked to 101 and 46 in the final and is part of the India ‘A’ squad, was born in the steel city of Bokaro. The Dhanbad-born 23-year-old offie Mohammed Kounain Quraishi cruised to 116 in the second innings while claiming the vital wicket of Varma. But Ranchi-born Shikhar Mohan was the stand-out newbie. The 21-year-old southpaw contributed with 85 and 52, displaying calm under pressure in the second innings. He was not only a livewire in the outfield but also stepped in as a left-arm spinner and claimed two wickets when senior Anukul Roy, another Jharkhand-born player, hurt his bowling finger.This was a team triumph. On pitches with different requirements, Bengal pacers Mukesh Kumar and Shami were better than their opposite numbers in both the semis and final. The tournament was a test for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s red-ball credentials. He demonstrated that he can adjust, even dominate. He remains a work in progress, especially against spin. The teenager must be evaluated not only by the runs he scores, but the way he scores them.Irrespective of where they ply their trade, players born in Bihar and Jharkhand are the fulcrum of the new rising East. There was a time when the zonal side was dominated by home-grown Bengal players. Barring Sudeep Gharami, every other player representing Bengal in the final’s playing XI was a cricket migrant.
Article Summary: South Zone were 19-time winners and East Zone had taken home the inter-zonal trophy only twice, the last in 2012-13. East outplayed the hosts in every area, including hunger and self-belief to win the trophy. Even the sparse Chennai crowd clapped for the visiting side.

Hockey India lauds Savita’s leadership and longevity

Savita Punia has etched her name into Indian hockey history, becoming the most-capped player in the history of the women’s national team. The veteran goalkeeper surpassed former India striker Vandana Katariya’s record of 320 senior international appearances during India’s Pool B match against Indonesia at the Asian Games in Japan, prompting Hockey India to announce a cash reward of Rs 10 lakh.Hockey India on Monday hailed Savita’s milestone as a testament to “two decades of discipline and leadership”, recognising the 36-year-old’s enduring contribution to the team.Known as ‘The Wall of India’ for her outstanding shot-stopping ability and composure in penalty shoot-outs, Savita made her senior international debut in 2009. Over the years, she has become one of the most dependable figures in Indian women’s hockey, featuring at three Olympic Games, two Asian Games, the Commonwealth Games, and several Asian Champions Trophy and FIH Pro League campaigns.She also served as captain of the Indian women’s team before Salima Tete took over the role.Savita reached her 300th international appearance in February 2025 against the Netherlands in the FIH Hockey Pro League. She became only the second Indian woman, after Vandana, to reach the milestone, and the second Indian goalkeeper, after PR Sreejesh, to do so.Savita equalled Vandana’s record of 320 appearances on September 20, 2026, during India’s 19-0 win over Uzbekistan in their Asian Games opener.She then moved past the mark in Monday’s match against Indonesia.Vandana, India’s all-time leading goal-scorer, made her international debut in the same year as Savita and retired in April 2025 after 320 appearances and 158 goals. Her career included a historic Olympic hat-trick at the Tokyo Games and the Padma Shri.Reflecting on the achievement, Savita thanked her family, coaches, teammates and everyone who supported her throughout her career.“I want to start by saying thank you, to my family, my coaches, my teammates and every single person who has stood behind me since I was a young girl learning to save my first penalty corner. Honestly, I never thought I would reach this milestone,” she said.Savita added that the record was shared with those who had been part of her journey, including Vandana, whose achievement had set a benchmark for Indian hockey.“This record doesn’t belong to me alone, it belongs to everyone who has played alongside me, and to Vandana too, because she set the bar and pushed all of us to reach higher,” she said.She also expressed hope that her achievement would encourage young players to keep working towards their dreams and represent India.Hockey India President Dilip Tirkey praised Savita’s consistency and leadership, saying her achievement reflected years of dedication to the sport.“Savita's record is a testament to two decades of discipline and quiet leadership. She has been the backbone of this team, and today's milestone is thoroughly deserved,” Tirkey said.
Article Summary: Savita Punia becomes country's most-capped women's hockey player. The veteran goalkeeper surpassed former India striker Vandana Katariya’s record of 320 senior international appearances. Hockey India announced a cash reward of Rs 10 lakh.

Article Title: Suchika Tariyal creates history, wins India's maiden MMA medal at Asian Games 2026

India's Suchika Tariyal (PTI Photo)

India’s Suchika Tariyal broke new ground in mixed martial arts at the Asian Games, but the historic moment came with heartbreak. The 36-year-old secured India’s maiden MMA medal at the continental showpiece on Monday, settling for bronze after losing a gruelling women’s traditional 60kg semi-final to Singapore’s Hui Hoon Teo in the extra round.Tariyal went down 0-2 in the extra round after a closely fought contest in which both fighters appeared exhausted, with neither able to land a decisive blow through their punches and kicks. While Teo celebrated her place in the final, an emotional Tariyal struggled to come to terms with the result, breaking down in tears as her coach consoled her.The bronze medal took India’s overall tally at the Games to four, with three silver medals having come from the shooting range.Despite the disappointment of missing out on a place in the final, Tariyal’s achievement marked a milestone for Indian sport, with MMA making its debut at the ongoing Asian Games.The Rohtak-born athlete had booked her place in the semi-finals with a 2-0 victory over Mongolia’s Altanchimeg Baigalmaa in the quarter-finals, thereby assuring herself of a medal.A former judoka, Tariyal represented India at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham and competed in kurash at the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou.Her bronze in Nagoya added another chapter to a sporting journey that has spanned multiple disciplines.Tariyal had also previously competed in MMA, making her professional debut in 2017 and winning her first bout. She then spent seven years away from the sport while pursuing judo and Jiu-Jitsu before returning to MMA competition and signing a multi-fight deal with BRAVE Combat Federation in November 2024.Her return came after overcoming setbacks, including a knee injury, while she also gained public recognition through an appearance on the television reality show Roadies.MMA is one of six sports making their Asian Games debut in Aichi-Nagoya, alongside freestyle BMX, teqball, padel, surfing and virtual taekwondo.

Article Title: India women's table tennis team stun Singapore in thrilling comeback as men suffer 0-3 loss at Asian Games

India’s table tennis campaign at the Asian Games began with contrasting results in the team events, with the women staging a remarkable comeback against Singapore while the men suffered a 0-3 defeat to Iran on Sunday. The Indian women, who had opened their campaign with a 3-0 win over Indonesia, came from 1-2 down to beat Singapore 3-2 in their second Group F tie at the Sky Hall Toyota. Yashaswini Ghorpade and Sreeja Akula held their nerve in the final two matches to seal the victory.India now have four points from their opening two ties and sit atop Group F. Yashaswini had put India ahead with a 3-1 win over Jian Zeng, but Singapore fought back as Sreeja lost a thrilling five-game contest to Ming Loy.Zhao Tan then beat Diya Chitale in four games to put Singapore 2-1 ahead.With India staring at defeat, Sreeja responded emphatically, recovering from losing the opening game 6-11 to beat her opponent 3-1. She won the next three games 11-3, 11-7, 11-4 to level the tie. Yashaswini then returned for the decider and showed considerable composure.After losing the opening game 5-11, she won the next two 11-8, 12-10 before Singapore forced a fifth with an 11-4 win.The final game went down to the wire, but Yashaswini held her nerve to win 11-9 and complete the comeback.Big medal hopes in doublesThe biggest expectations are centred around Manush Shah and Diya Chitale in mixed doubles, while Manav Thakkar and Manush Shah will carry significant hopes in the men’s doubles. Both combinations have spent the year competing against some of the best pairs and have been ranked among the world’s top five.The depth within the Indian contingent is also a reflection of how much the sport has grown in the country. Four of the five members of both the men’s and women’s teams are ranked inside the world’s top 100. But Asia remains the toughest examination in table tennis, with China, Japan, South Korea and Chinese Taipei providing a formidable presence.

CHENNAI: Indian-origin all-rounder Sabaorish Ravichandran has represented Japan on the global stage for the past four years. So they thought it would be better to use the existing Asian Games squad.I’m not part of the Asian Games squad because I don’t possess a Japanese passport,” he added.There was a sense of missing out for Sabaorish, especially because the India-Japan fixture was not something he had seen coming when he decided to move back to Chennai. The discussions about relocating had begun last Sept, and he knew he would miss the Games because of the passport rule. But a bilateral match against India was a different proposition altogether. He admitted he was “really, really down” when the news broke, knowing the occasion could have given him and the Japan team a chance to be noticed.“Sometimes it’s just life, right? Some 50km away, at the makeshift cricket stadium inside Korogi Sports Park, another delayed milestone was being achieved by prodigal opener Shafali Verma.The Indian opener ended a seven-year wait for a white-ball century on Sunday, smashing an unbeaten 49-ball 100 (3x4, 9x6) to power defending champions India into Tuesday’s final against Sri Lanka.India crushed Bangladesh by 114 runs in a one-sided semifinal after posting 194/4, with Shafali anchoring the innings. Earlier, in a rain-affected semifinal, Sri Lanka eased past Pakistan by eight wickets.Shafali and Smriti Mandhana (37) gave India a flying start with a 72-run opening stand. In the process, Smriti became the highest run-scorer in women’s T20 internationals, taking her tally to 4,788 runs and surpassing New Zealand’s Suzie Bates (4,758).India also had reason to cheer with their captain finding rhythm. Harmanpreet Kaur, who hasn’t had a great run with the bat, struck a 33-ball 40. Bangladesh never threatened in the chase and were bowled out for 81 in 15.4 overs, with Nandini Sharma and Deepti Sharma taking three wickets apiece.For Shafali, though, the afternoon was about finally breaking a barrier that had stood since her T20I debut in 2019. It took her 118 matches to get there.The 22-year-old, who was under the weather, showed no signs of discomfort once she found her rhythm, hitting a boundary and a six off Sanjida Akter in the second over.“This century is very special because from the time I started playing cricket, I’ve manifested scoring a T20 century. I know it took me a long time, but I’m happy that it’s finally come,” a visibly relieved Shafali said.“When I debuted for the team in 2019, I thought T20 was my favourite format and I would put up a show in it, but it took some years for that,” she added.Shafali said she had mixed caution with aggression and rotated the strike, after India’s easy quarterfinal against Japan had left several players short of match practice. “The deliveries which were not in the range, I wanted to play them down. I was also focused on rotating strike so that the others get used to the conditions as well,” she said.
Article Summary: India crushed Bangladesh by 114 runs in a one-sided semifinal after posting 194/4. Earlier, in a rain-affected semifinal, Sri Lanka eased past Pakistan by eight wickets. Shafali and Smriti Mandhana gave India a flying start with a 72-run opening stand.

Article Title: She once fought harassment; now Suchika Tariyal assures India an MMA medal at Asian Games 2026
Article Text:
Suchika Tariyal assured India’s first medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games (Image: ANI)

TimesofIndia in Nagoya:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What began as a journey of self-defence has taken 36-year-old Suchika Tariyal to the podium, in a sport that is not only new to the Games but also relatively new to her.While athletes from more established disciplines were looking to open India’s medal account on Sunday, the multifaceted Suchika carved out a piece of history, assuring the country of a medal in the traditional 60kg MMA category.She defeated Mongolia’s Altanchimeg Baigalmaa 2-0 in the quarterfinals to book her place in the last four, where she will face Singapore’s Hoon Hui Teo.The route to the podium has been an arduous one for the Rohtak-born athlete.A victim of harassment as a child, Suchika refused to be cowed by those experiences. Instead, they became a motivation to make herself physically and mentally stronger.She represented India in judo at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham and the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games, where she competed in kurash, before being crowned world champion in ju-jitsu in 2024. Her first brush with MMA came in 2017, but she returned to the sport only in 2024.Growing up in a conservative family in Haryana, Suchika had to overcome societal pressures and social barriers to pursue her sporting ambitions. From being a self-trained athlete, she went on to become an eight-time national judo champion. She later appeared on a reality show and ventured into professional MMA fights before switching to the amateur circuit with the Asian Games in her sights.“I’m thrilled that I have assured my country a medal. I hope I will fight for the gold. Although I’ve been an athlete since childhood, it has taken a long time to get here,” said Suchika, who works as a junior coach with the Haryana sports department.Suchika, a largely self-funded athlete, who is still paying off loans taken to pursue her passion, believes her years as a judoka have provided the foundation for her MMA journey.
Article Summary: Suchika Tariyal assured India’s first medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. The 36-year-old won a gold medal in the traditional 60kg MMA category. Suchika will face Singapore's Hoon Hui Teo in the last four.

Article Title: Asian Games 2026: India clinch silver in men’s 10m air rifle team event
Article Text:
Dehradun: From left to right, Maharashtra's Rudrankksh Patil and Parth Rakesh Mane (PTI Photo)

Rudrankksh, Himanshu qualify for individual final

China break world record to clinch gold

India’s shooting medal streak continued at the Asian Games on Monday, with Rudrankksh Patil, Himanshu Dhillon and Parth Mane clinching silver in the men’s 10m air rifle team event. The trio shot a combined 1890.1 points to secure India’s first medal of the day, while Rudrankksh and Himanshu also qualified for the individual final.The Indian trio aggregated 1890.1 points to secure the silver medal, while China claimed gold with a world-record score of 1899.0. South Korea finished third to take bronze with a total of 1884.2 points.The qualification round also saw two Indian shooters book their places in the men’s 10m air rifle individual final.Rudrankksh led the Indian challenge, finishing third in the qualification standings with an impressive score of 631.8 points. Himanshu also progressed to the final after securing seventh place with 630.0 points. Parth, meanwhile, narrowly missed out on a place in the individual final, finishing 10th overall with a score of 628.3 points.China, featuring Olympic champion Sheng Lihao alongside Ma Sihan and Zhang Changhong, produced a commanding performance to claim the gold medal with a combined score of 1899.0 points, setting a new qualification world record.The men’s team silver added to India’s strong start in shooting at the Games. The women’s 10m air rifle team of Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod had also secured silver on the opening day, with Elavenil subsequently adding another silver in the individual event.India had finished with a record 22-medal haul in shooting at the Hangzhou Asian Games, winning seven gold, nine silver and six bronze medals.
Article Summary: Rudrankksh Patil, Himanshu Dhillon and Parth Mane claim silver in men's 10m air rifle team event. The Indian trio shot a combined 1890.1 points to secure the silver medal. China claimed gold with a world-record score of 1899.0. South Korea finished third to take bronze with a total of 1884.2.

Article Title: Neck pillows, no screen time and changing lights: How shooters are tackling conditions at Quaint
Article Text:
India's shooting contingent (ANI Image)

TimesofIndia in Nagoya:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

There’s a running joke among members of the Indian shooting contingent that the bus ride from their hotel in central Nagoya to the Aichi Prefectural General Shooting Gallery feels like a journey through the bends and turns leading up to Ooty in the Nilgiris.The range, about 75km from their hotel, is the farthest the shooters say, they have had to travel to a venue at an international event. The journey takes close to two hours.“The organisers told us the travel time would be 70 minutes, but it’s about two hours. Given how punctual the Japanese are, we took it at face value. We wish they had told us the actual travel time. We would have been mentally prepared for it,” said Manoj Kumar Ohlyan, chief coach of the 50m rifle team.The shooters, coaches and support staff have since put a few coping mechanisms in place. Most use travel neck pillows to stay comfortable on the winding roads, while screen time is strictly prohibited.“Screen time during such long travel can cause motion sickness, so we tell the shooters they can use their mobiles only to listen to music and not watch anything,” Ohlyan said. Elavenil Valarivan , who suffered a disc bulge in her neck a few years ago, is taking no chances.After winning two silver medals on Sunday, she said, “It’s a long ride to the range and, given my history with the neck, I ensure I travel here with a neck pillow.”The distance, however, is not the only challenge. Ohlyan said the altitude (sitting at an elevation of 670m or nearly 2,200 feet) at the relatively compact range has little bearing on the shooters, but changing light conditions could prove tricky.“The lighting can sometimes be tricky because it is mostly cloudy now. But when there is brighter light, there is a likelihood of a mirage forming when the 50m rifle shooters are in action. So we have discussed the scenarios and made adjustments accordingly,” he said.Team high-performance manager and former shooter Ronak Pandit explained that a change in weather can also affect the shooters psychologically.“Unfortunately, on the day of the match, if we have sunny conditions, the calibration of the rifle changes. Also, here the athletes are trained to shoot in the wind. What could happen is that when you are under pressure and the conditions also go against you, it impacts you psychologically,” Pandit said.“That said, all the shooters are experienced, well-travelled and well-coached. So hopefully, we will be least affected if the conditions change,” he added.
Article Summary: The journey to the range takes close to two hours. Most use travel neck pillows to stay comfortable on the winding roads. Screen time is strictly prohibited. The altitude (sitting at an elevation of 670m or nearly 2,200 feet) at the relatively compact range could prove tricky.

Article Title: 'I did my absolute best': Elavenil’s golden dream falls short, but double silver ends eight-year Asian Games wait
Article Text:
Elavenil Valarivan (ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The gold was within touching distance — a mere 0.6 points away. But after leading for much of the 10m air rifle final, Elavenil Valarivan , India’s shooting super star in the making for almost a decade, had to settle for silver.At the Aichi Prefectural General Shooting Gallery on a Sunday afternoon, Elavenil provided India’s individual silver lining, while the trio of Elavenil, Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod added another silver in the team event.China set a world record of 1904.2 to win the team gold, with India second with 1898, bettering the previous Asian Games record of 1896.6. Hosts Japan took bronze with a score of 1897.1.In the individual final, the 27-year-old made a confident start and, at one stage, held a 1.5-point lead. But as the final entered its business end, the Indian admitted to having “relaxed a bit”, and the gold slipped away.The final was a pulsating affair. Elavenil, who had looked composed throughout, saw her lead disappear late on. With one final shot to come, she produced a 10.1 to finish on 252.4, narrowly missing out on gold. Japan’s Hinata Taichi finished with a flourish, shooting a total of 253 to win the gold and better the Games record of 252.7.Elavenil’s infectious smile wavered briefly. But the overriding expression on her face was relief.After all, these medals had been eight years in the making.If there were nerves, Elavenil did not show them. As she entered the final, she appeared focused and almost oblivious to the competition, which included South Korea’s Olympic and world champion Ban Hyo-jin, who settled for bronze.The teenager who burst onto the scene almost a decade ago has endured more than her share of heartbreak on the biggest stages. Her Asian Games debut in Jakarta in 2018 ended in an anticlimax after a rifle malfunction, while she failed to make the finals at both the Tokyo and Paris Olympics.Those difficult years, she said, were “important for consistency over the years”.On missing out on gold, Elavenil was candid.“I really need to work on my finals more. I knew that I was in the top three. Although I was coming back to focusing on my process and my technique, I did get a bit relaxed. Once the medal was assured, the pressure was released. It was more about me getting a little easy on my process,” she said.“I felt I gave my absolute best and I am glad that it turned out this way,” she added.Elavenil has been on a roll over the past 15 months, with podium finishes at the Asian Championships, World Championships and the Munich World Cup.“I am very grateful that I have been getting many opportunities to learn and experiment and utilise my potential to my absolute best,” she said.As she was being ushered into the press conference, Elavenil pulled out her phone and called her coach Neha Chavan. With the two silver medals around her neck, she flashed her brightest smile.“Ma’am, I just wanted to show the medals to you,” she said.After the press conference, she did the same with her mentor Gagan Narang, who, incidentally, had won silver in the corresponding men’s events at the 2010 Asian Games.Neha may not have been there to watch her climb the podium, but her words stayed with Elavenil.“You have trained your best. There’s nothing more you can do on the day. All I can wish for you is to follow the technique, trust yourself and be courageous, as you have always been,” Neha had told her, Elavenil revealed.Before heading into the final, Elavenil had pulled out her diary. She wrote just one line: “I did my absolute best.”Before she could write more, she was called into the arena.
Article Summary: India's Elavenil Valarivan won silver in the 10m air rifle final. The 27-year- old led for much of the final, but saw her lead disappear late on. China set a world record of 1904.2 to win the team gold, with India second with 1898. Hosts Japan took bronze with a score of 1897.1.

Article Title: Horrific! Former England footballer Andros Townsend run over by pitch roller in freak accident - Watch

Former England international Andros Townsend was involved in a freak accident during the warm-up before his Thai League One side PT Prachuap’s match against Pattani FC, appearing to be struck and briefly run over by a pitch roller.Footage circulating on social media, reportedly from the warm-up, shows Townsend attempting an acrobatic backheel while jumping for the ball as the grounds vehicle moves towards him. The roller appears to collide with the 35-year-old before passing over him as he lies on his side.The driver then appears to get out of the vehicle and attempt to tilt it to one side, allowing Townsend to free himself. He also represented England at international level.Townsend's most recent club in England was Luton Town. He left the Championship side in 2024 to join Turkish club Antalyaspor before continuing his career in Thailand.After moving to his second Thai club, Townsend described the move as his “Thai adventure” continuing. However, the latest chapter proved far more dramatic than expected, with the former Premier League winger finding himself involved in an unusual pitch-side accident.The incident occurred before the match and, despite the collision, Townsend was able to take part in the game later that night.
